scenario: Adopt Lintwise as a required pre-merge check (eight engineers)

motion.text: The team adopts Lintwise, an automated code-quality checker, as a required pre-merge check on every repository.

research: Marcus: Measure Lintwise wall-clock runtime on our actual monorepo and confirm whether it can execute as a parallel CI job alongside compilation rather than as a serial pre-build gate. Report the added latency in seconds and whether it stays under the 60-second threshold.

Sana: Run Lintwise against a representative slice of our SQL queries and Python pipeline scripts for a short trial. Report the false-positive rate on those languages specifically, so we can determine whether the JavaScript noise figure (~30 %) generalises or whether SQL/Python need a separate, narrower rule set before the gate is made mandatory.

chairQuestions.topic: False-positive rate and rule tuning over six months of Lintwise use
chairQuestions.experience_sought: In your six months running Lintwise, roughly what fraction of flagged issues were genuine bugs versus stylistic or intentional-trade-off noise, and how often did you adjust or disable rules to keep the signal-to-noise ratio acceptable for the team?

chairQuestions.topic: Specific false positives and rule categories encountered in your three-week Lintwise trial
chairQuestions.experience_sought: You mentioned Lintwise flagged intentional trade-offs in your React project. Can you recall which rule categories produced those false positives—stylistic, accessibility, async-pattern—and whether you could suppress them per-file or only globally?
